items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: We were at Stay Phillips. And we were recording Frankie Valli with the Four Seasons.

ctx.x: Who would be sitting next to you on dates like that?

Well you’re going to interview Eddie Bert later on today. Eddie and I have done a lot of work together. We had a very funny situation. I remember this better than Eddie which is unusual because Eddie has got a memory like a steel trap and he’s accurate. But this I remember well. We were at Stay Phillips. And we were recording Frankie Valli with the Four Seasons. Well it wasn’t even Frankie Valli in those days, it was just simply The Four Seasons. And we were sitting as a band, they had an isolation booth for the…

Okay. [scats] “No Frank, you have to start earlier.” And by this time he’s getting into a panic. You know the eyes are starting to get wide. It must have gone on for it seemed like a long time, it was probably about ten minutes or so. And on recording time, where time is money, you know ten minutes of wasting time like that you start getting nervous. And they were getting very nervous in the booth. Eddie and I were — Eddie is very cool. He was just sort of sitting there you know and I was digging the whole thing.…
